chapter: Postwar clubs, Chile and New York
title: East St. Louis jazz policy gig with Ruby Braff and Bob Wilber
summary: Freeman takes Ruby Braff, Paul Jordan and Bob Wilber to a new East St. Louis jazz club, needing a drummer before opening.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And then I -- let's see, oh, yes, then I got an offer to go to East St. Louis to play a club that was starting a jazz policy and I took Ruby Braff with me and a fellow by the name of Paul Jordan, who was a wonderful composer, do you remember, pianist-composer, and we didn't have a drummer so we couldn't go on for the opening night until we got a drummer, who turned out to be very good and there again, it's difficult to remember the other people. Oh, Bob Wilbur played clarinet.
He did, some of the earliest times that Bob Wilbur was heard.
Well, Bob Wilbur -- I don't remember
He hadn't had too much exposure by then.
I don't think he had had too much, but he was a marvelous player.
Yes, he might have played at Eddie's or I think it was later when he played at Eddie's. It's difficult to remember that.
